name: Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:   # execução manual

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "Rodando CI (lint, build, testes unitários)"

  cd:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: ci
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "Rodando CD (deploy, push de imagem)"

  k8s-matrix:
    # aqui você define que vai rodar no runner self-hosted
    runs-on: self-hosted
    needs: [ci, cd]
    strategy:
      matrix:
        db: [mysql, postgres, sqlite]
        k8s_version: [1.24.0, 1.25.0]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup kubectl
        uses: azure/setup-kubectl@v3
        with:
          version: ${{ matrix.k8s_version }}

      - name: Configure kubeconfig
        run: |
          echo "$KUBECONFIG_CONTENT" > $HOME/.kube/config

      - name: Deploy database pod
        run: |
          kubectl apply -f k8s/db/${{ matrix.db }}.yaml
          kubectl rollout status deployment/${{ matrix.db }}-db

      - name: Deploy application
        run: |
          kubectl apply -f k8s/app/deployment.yaml
          kubectl rollout status deployment/myapp

      - name: Run integration tests
        run: |
          kubectl exec deploy/myapp -- npm run test:integration -- --db ${{ matrix.db }}

      - name: Cleanup
        if: always()
        run: |
          kubectl delete -f k8s/db/${{ matrix.db }}.yaml
          kubectl delete -f k8s/app/deployment.yaml




# job k8s-matrix agora usa runs-on: self-hosted.

#Isso significa que ele não vai rodar nos runners do GitHub, mas sim no runner que você registrou (sua VM, servidor ou máquina local).

#Continua sendo manual (workflow_dispatch), então você dispara quando quiser.
